speaker: Mikel Arteta
quote_text:
Yeah, I was very happy, obviously, with the  results with big parts of that performance. I love  
the attitude of the team from the beginning, the  way we approach it, how aggressive we were with  
the ball, score a goal, have a lot of chances that  we didn’t put away. And then, yeah, we continue  
to do a lot of the things defensively so well that  are in the right to attack open spaces and so many  
situations of huge advantages that we just gave  away. And then we have to track back 17 metres  
and on that phase probably we’ve been one of  the best teams in the world today because we  
were unbelievable the way we’ve done it. And we  haven’t conceded almost nothing apart from that  
save from David, I would say. And that’s a big  credit to the team because in my opinion they  
are the best attacking team in the league. If you  avoid defeat at Liverpool later in the season,  
this is for the second season in a row, you’ve not  lost a game against the traditional big six in the  
league. What does that say about the team? Yeah,  that we are capable of competing consistently  
with really high standards again, any kind of  opposition, and if we continue to do those things,  
we’ll get rewarded. I think so. And the set-piece  goals are back. Yeah. Well, and that was some  
header. I mean, as we worked on that, that  looked quite acrobatic. We work on something  
similar with that finish, you know, to be fair,  it was a different kind of finish planned,  
but very happy because that will generate  belief in the team again, even the stadium,  
the crowd, that we can score because it’s  something that we’re missing, obviously,  
when we’ve been so prolific on that front with  the amount of injuries that we had up front,  
so very, very happy with that. Merino, it doesn’t  seem to be a very like a happy centre-forward,  
but he’s kind of playing, you know, he says  he’ll play there for you, but you know,  
he seems to be playing himself into a job, you  know, every week, right? And we know that that  
was the emergency situation that we are in at  the moment, but the way he’s approaching it is  
incredible. He wants to understand everything.  He wants to learn from it. He’s very critical of  
himself all the time. And at the end, the reality  is that he’s winning football matches for us,  
which is incredible. He’s never played in that  position before in his life. And some of the  
goals he’s scored are quite spectacular, and that  one today as well. Yeah, and the value of it,  
you know, it’s a big match. At the end, you win  the game because of that goal. He had another  
big chance that almost put the ball in the back  of the net. So very happy with his contribution.  
You said they’re the best attacking team in the  league. Yeah, in open play, yes, by a mile. I  
mean, the stats say it and everything that I’ve  seen them do. They can open you up, they can run  
in transition, they have individual quality.  Any player in the defensive line can throw  
you in behind, they can combine on both sides, on  weak side, and they are missing some big players  
as well at the moment. Do you feel next season  they’re going to be a major threat? Yeah, and I  
think they won’t have to play Thursday, Saturday  and the amount of injuries that they had as well.  
They were on the edge because of the manager that  they have, who is really good, and the players  
and the squad, obviously, the quality that they  have. Just on the Chelsea point, is that people’s  
perception of Chelsea on the outside is that maybe  they struggle to create chances in this territory  
without actually penetrating? Is this a difference  between you as a manager and fans seeing Chelsea  
in a different way? I don’t know. It’s my  opinion. I have a lot of data, the objective one,  
what it says, and as well what I see in the  games that they play. But I might be wrong.  
I don’t know. It’s just yourself setting up to  play against these big teams. We spoke about the  
record and not conceding any chances. Is it quite  refreshing for you to set up your teams to maybe  
soak up pressure rather than playing against more  blocks every week? Yeah, but I would like to see a  
different score line, to be fair, with the amount  of things that we do so well, the end product  
there has to improve because the moment we do  that, you are very far away from the position.  
Is 12 points manageable? Can you rein in Liverpool  with a 12-point gap? We have to win our remaining  
matches, that’s why we have to win against Fulham  and we will be closer. Yeah, thank you. Thank you.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Arsenal 1-0 Chelsea
